description: Comprehensive question bank on Environmental Problems and Development Issues of Karnataka - Forests (FDA & SDA Exam-Oriented). Based on Karnataka Forests study material covering forest resources, deforestation, afforestation, forest conservation and forest fires. All questions verified against the source document.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a forest?

options.A: An area with only trees and no other organisms
options.B: An ecosystem dominated by trees and other woody vegetation, together with associated plants, animals, microorganisms, soil, water and ecological processes
options.C: Land legally notified as forest by the government only
options.D: A plantation of a single tree species

questions.explanation: A forest is an ecosystem dominated by trees and other woody vegetation, together with associated plants, animals, microorganisms, soil, water and ecological processes. The precise statistical definition of forest varies between countries and reporting systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is forest cover in India's Forest Survey of India assessment?

options.A: Land of one hectare or more with tree canopy density of 10 per cent or more, irrespective of ownership, legal status or land use
options.B: Only land legally notified as forest
options.C: Land with tree canopy density of 40 per cent or more
options.D: Land recorded as forest in government records

questions.explanation: Forest cover is land of one hectare or more with tree canopy density of 10 per cent or more, irrespective of ownership, legal status or land use; it can therefore include plantations and tree patches outside legally recorded forests.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is very dense forest (VDF) in the Forest Survey of India classification?

options.A: Forest cover with canopy density of 40 per cent or more but less than 70 per cent
options.B: Forest cover with canopy density of 10 per cent or more but less than 40 per cent
options.C: Forest cover with canopy density of 70 per cent or more
options.D: Land with canopy density below 10 per cent

questions.explanation: Very dense forest is forest cover with canopy density of 70 per cent or more.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is moderately dense forest (MDF) in the Forest Survey of India classification?

options.A: Forest cover with canopy density of 70 per cent or more
options.B: Forest cover with canopy density of 40 per cent or more but less than 70 per cent
options.C: Forest cover with canopy density of 10 per cent or more but less than 40 per cent
options.D: Land with canopy density below 10 per cent

questions.explanation: Moderately dense forest is forest cover with canopy density of 40 per cent or more but less than 70 per cent.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is open forest (OF) in the Forest Survey of India classification?

options.A: Forest cover with canopy density of 70 per cent or more
options.B: Forest cover with canopy density of 40 per cent or more but less than 70 per cent
options.C: Forest cover with canopy density of 10 per cent or more but less than 40 per cent
options.D: Land with canopy density below 10 per cent

questions.explanation: Open forest is forest cover with canopy density of 10 per cent or more but less than 40 per cent.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is scrub in the Forest Survey of India classification?

options.A: Forest cover with canopy density of 10 per cent or more but less than 40 per cent
options.B: Land with canopy density below 10 per cent, generally showing poor or degraded tree growth
options.C: Forest cover with canopy density of 70 per cent or more
options.D: Land recorded as forest in government records

questions.explanation: Scrub is land with canopy density below 10 per cent, generally showing poor or degraded tree growth; it is reported separately from forest cover.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is tree cover?

options.A: Land legally notified as forest
options.B: Tree patches outside the mapped forest-cover category, including small patches and scattered trees, as assessed under the Forest Survey of India methodology
options.C: Forest cover with canopy density of 70 per cent or more
options.D: Land with canopy density below 10 per cent

questions.explanation: Tree cover generally refers to tree patches outside the mapped forest-cover category, including small patches and scattered trees, as assessed under the Forest Survey of India methodology.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is recorded forest area?

options.A: Land with tree canopy density of 10 per cent or more
options.B: Land recorded as forest in government records, irrespective of whether it currently has tree canopy
options.C: Tree patches outside the mapped forest-cover category
options.D: Land with canopy density of 70 per cent or more

questions.explanation: Recorded forest area is land recorded as forest in government records, irrespective of whether it currently has tree canopy; it is a legal or administrative land category, not the same as measured forest cover.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is canopy density?

options.A: The total number of trees in a forest
options.B: The proportion of ground covered by the vertical projection of tree crowns, expressed as a percentage
options.C: The height of the tallest tree in a forest

questions.explanation: Canopy density is the proportion of ground covered by the vertical projection of tree crowns, expressed as a percentage.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is natural forest?

options.A: A forest established by planting or deliberate seeding
options.B: An ecosystem that has developed primarily through natural regeneration and ecological processes
options.C: A forest with only one tree species

questions.explanation: A natural forest is an ecosystem that has developed primarily through natural regeneration and ecological processes, although many natural forests may also have experienced human disturbance.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a plantation forest?

options.A: A forest that has developed through natural regeneration
options.B: An area established by planting or deliberate seeding, often with one or a limited number of tree species
options.C: Land with canopy density below 10 per cent
options.D: A forest with only native species

questions.explanation: A plantation forest is an area established by planting or deliberate seeding, often with one or a limited number of tree species, for ecological restoration, timber, pulp, fuelwood or other purposes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a tropical evergreen forest?

options.A: A forest where all trees shed their leaves during a dry season
options.B: A dense, multi-layered forest in high-rainfall areas where trees generally remain green throughout the year and do not shed all their leaves in one common season
options.C: A dry vegetation type dominated by thorny shrubs
options.D: A forest that grows in intertidal coastal environments

questions.explanation: A tropical evergreen forest is a dense, multi-layered forest in high-rainfall areas where trees generally remain green throughout the year and do not shed all their leaves in one common season.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests found in Karnataka?

options.A: In the drier interior and eastern parts of Karnataka
options.B: In the high-rainfall Western Ghats, especially in parts of Uttara Kannada, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru and Kodagu districts
options.C: In the rain-shadow areas of north Karnataka

questions.explanation: Tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests are prominent in the high-rainfall Western Ghats, especially in parts of Uttara Kannada, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru and Kodagu districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a moist deciduous forest?

options.A: A dense, multi-layered forest where trees remain green throughout the year
options.B: A tropical forest in which many trees shed their leaves during a dry season, but rainfall is sufficient to support relatively dense vegetation
options.C: A dry vegetation type dominated by thorny shrubs
options.D: A forest that grows in intertidal coastal environments

questions.explanation: A moist deciduous forest is a tropical forest in which many trees shed their leaves during a dry season, but rainfall is sufficient to support relatively dense vegetation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are moist deciduous forests found in Karnataka?

options.A: In the high-rainfall Western Ghats only
options.B: In parts of the Western Ghats and adjoining regions, including areas of the Malnad and the wetter forest belts of the State
options.C: In the drier districts and rain-shadow areas
options.D: In the eastern Deccan plateau only

questions.explanation: Moist deciduous forests occur in parts of the Western Ghats and adjoining regions, including areas of the Malnad and the wetter forest belts of the State.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a dry deciduous forest?

options.A: A dense forest where trees remain green throughout the year
options.B: A forest that occurs in areas with a pronounced dry season and lower rainfall than moist deciduous forests, where many trees shed leaves during the dry months
options.C: A forest that grows in intertidal coastal environments
options.D: A forest found only in high-altitude valleys

questions.explanation: A dry deciduous forest occurs in areas with a pronounced dry season and lower rainfall than moist deciduous forests; many trees shed leaves during the dry months.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are dry deciduous forests found in Karnataka?

options.A: In the high-rainfall Western Ghats
options.B: In the drier interior and eastern parts of Karnataka, including portions of the Deccan plateau and the forest landscapes around Bandipur and other eastern forest divisions
options.C: In the estuarine systems of the western coast
options.D: In high-altitude valleys of the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Dry deciduous forests occur in the drier interior and eastern parts of Karnataka, including portions of the Deccan plateau and the forest landscapes around Bandipur and other eastern forest divisions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a thorn forest?

options.A: A dense forest where trees remain green throughout the year
options.B: A dry vegetation type dominated by thorny shrubs and drought-resistant trees, commonly found in areas of low and irregular rainfall
options.C: A forest that grows in intertidal coastal environments
options.D: A forest found only in high-altitude valleys

questions.explanation: A thorn forest is a dry vegetation type dominated by thorny shrubs and drought-resistant trees, commonly found in areas of low and irregular rainfall.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are thorn and scrub forests found in Karnataka?

options.A: In the high-rainfall Western Ghats
options.B: In drier districts and rain-shadow areas, including parts of north and central Karnataka and the eastern Deccan plateau
options.C: In the estuarine systems of the western coast
options.D: In high-altitude valleys of the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Thorn and scrub forests are characteristic of drier districts and rain-shadow areas, including parts of north and central Karnataka and the eastern Deccan plateau.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are mangrove forests?

options.A: Dense, multi-layered forests in high-rainfall areas
options.B: Salt-tolerant trees and shrubs that grow in intertidal coastal environments, stabilise shorelines and provide nursery habitats for fish and other organisms
options.C: Dry vegetation dominated by thorny shrubs
options.D: Patches of stunted evergreen montane forest found in high-altitude valleys

questions.explanation: Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees and shrubs that grow in intertidal coastal environments, stabilise shorelines and provide nursery habitats for fish and other organisms.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are mangroves found in Karnataka?

options.A: In the drier interior and eastern parts of Karnataka
options.B: In estuaries and sheltered coastal stretches of Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts, including parts of the Kali, Sharavathi, Netravati and other estuarine systems
options.C: In high-altitude valleys of the Western Ghats
options.D: In the rain-shadow areas of north Karnataka

questions.explanation: Mangroves occur in estuaries and sheltered coastal stretches of Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts, including parts of the Kali, Sharavathi, Netravati and other estuarine systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are shola forests?

options.A: Salt-tolerant trees and shrubs that grow in intertidal coastal environments
options.B: Patches of stunted evergreen montane forest found in high-altitude valleys, often forming a mosaic with montane grasslands in the southern Western Ghats
options.C: Dry vegetation dominated by thorny shrubs
options.D: Dense, multi-layered forests in high-rainfall areas

questions.explanation: Shola forests are patches of stunted evergreen montane forest found in high-altitude valleys, often forming a mosaic with montane grasslands in the southern Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are shola-grassland ecosystems found in Karnataka?

options.A: In the drier interior and eastern parts of Karnataka
options.B: In high-elevation landscapes of the Western Ghats, including parts of Kudremukh and adjoining high ranges
options.C: In estuaries and sheltered coastal stretches
options.D: In the rain-shadow areas of north Karnataka

questions.explanation: Shola-grassland ecosystems occur in high-elevation landscapes of the Western Ghats, including parts of Kudremukh and adjoining high ranges.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are forest resources?

options.A: Only timber obtained from forests
options.B: The useful products, ecosystem services and ecological functions obtained from forests, including timber, fuelwood, fodder, bamboo, medicinal plants, fruits, fibres, water regulation, soil protection and biodiversity
options.D: Only the land area recorded as forest

questions.explanation: Forest resources are the useful products, ecosystem services and ecological functions obtained from forests, including timber, fuelwood, fodder, bamboo, medicinal plants, fruits, fibres, water regulation, soil protection and biodiversity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are timber forest products?

options.A: Forest products other than timber, such as bamboo and honey
options.B: Wood materials used for construction, furniture, poles, plywood, paper and other industrial or domestic purposes, subject to forest laws and sustainable-harvest rules
options.C: Only firewood collected by local communities
options.D: Medicinal plants and fruits from forests

questions.explanation: Timber products are wood materials used for construction, furniture, poles, plywood, paper and other industrial or domestic purposes, subject to forest laws and sustainable-harvest rules.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs)?

options.A: Wood materials used for construction and furniture
options.B: Forest products other than timber, such as bamboo, cane, tendu leaves, honey, wax, medicinal plants, gums, resins, fruits, seeds, fibres and leaves

questions.explanation: NTFPs are forest products other than timber, such as bamboo, cane, tendu leaves, honey, wax, medicinal plants, gums, resins, fruits, seeds, fibres and leaves.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why are NTFPs important to forest-dependent communities?

options.A: They provide only timber for construction
options.B: They provide food, medicines, household materials and seasonal income, particularly for many Adivasi and other forest-dependent communities
options.C: They are used only for industrial purposes
options.D: They are exported only to other countries

questions.explanation: NTFPs provide food, medicines, household materials and seasonal income, particularly for many Adivasi and other forest-dependent communities; sustainable harvesting and fair market access are important.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the major ecological services provided by forests?

options.A: Only timber production
options.B: Forests store carbon, regulate local and regional water cycles, protect soil, reduce erosion, support pollination, recycle nutrients, moderate local climate, provide habitat and maintain biodiversity

questions.explanation: Forests store carbon, regulate local and regional water cycles, protect soil, reduce erosion, support pollination, recycle nutrients, moderate local climate, provide habitat and maintain biodiversity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How do forests help in soil conservation?

options.A: By increasing surface runoff
options.B: Tree roots bind soil, canopy and leaf litter reduce the impact of raindrops, and forest vegetation slows surface runoff, thereby reducing erosion and landslides
options.C: By removing all vegetation from the soil surface
options.D: By increasing the speed of water flow

questions.explanation: Tree roots bind soil, canopy and leaf litter reduce the impact of raindrops, and forest vegetation slows surface runoff, thereby reducing erosion and landslides.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How do forests contribute to water conservation?

options.A: By increasing rapid surface runoff
options.B: Forests intercept rainfall, improve infiltration, maintain soil structure, regulate runoff and help sustain springs, streams and river flows, although the effect varies with forest type, soil, climate and land use
options.C: By preventing all rainfall from reaching the ground

questions.explanation: Forests intercept rainfall, improve infiltration, maintain soil structure, regulate runoff and help sustain springs, streams and river flows, although the effect varies with forest type, soil, climate and land use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How do forests help regulate climate?

options.A: By releasing all stored carbon into the atmosphere
options.B: Forests absorb and store carbon dioxide through photosynthesis and store carbon in vegetation and soils; they also influence evapotranspiration, shade and local temperature

questions.explanation: Forests absorb and store carbon dioxide through photosynthesis and store carbon in vegetation and soils; they also influence evapotranspiration, shade and local temperature.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is carbon sequestration by forests?

options.A: The release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
options.B: The capture and long-term storage of atmospheric carbon dioxide in trees, vegetation, dead organic matter and forest soils
options.D: The removal of all trees from a forest

questions.explanation: Carbon sequestration is the capture and long-term storage of atmospheric carbon dioxide in trees, vegetation, dead organic matter and forest soils.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is biodiversity?

options.A: The number of trees in a forest
options.B: The variability among living organisms from all sources, including diversity within species, between species and of ecosystems
options.C: The total area of a forest
options.D: The height of trees in a forest

questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variability among living organisms from all sources, including diversity within species, between species and of ecosystems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why are forests important for biodiversity?

options.A: They provide only timber
options.B: Forests provide food, shelter, breeding sites and ecological connections for plants, animals, fungi and microorganisms, supporting complex food webs and genetic diversity
options.C: They reduce the number of species

questions.explanation: Forests provide food, shelter, breeding sites and ecological connections for plants, animals, fungi and microorganisms, supporting complex food webs and genetic diversity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is a wildlife corridor?

options.A: A fence that prevents animal movement
options.B: A strip or landscape connection that allows animals and plants to move between habitat patches, supporting dispersal, migration and genetic exchange
options.C: A protected area where no human activity is allowed
options.D: A zoo where animals are kept

questions.explanation: A wildlife corridor is a strip or landscape connection that allows animals and plants to move between habitat patches, supporting dispersal, migration and genetic exchange.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is human-wildlife conflict?

options.A: When wildlife and human activities overlap in ways that cause harm to people, crops, livestock, property or wildlife
options.B: When humans and wildlife live in complete separation
options.C: When wildlife is kept in zoos

questions.explanation: Human-wildlife conflict occurs when wildlife and human activities overlap in ways that cause harm to people, crops, livestock, property or wildlife.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the role of forests in the livelihoods of Karnataka's rural communities?

options.A: Forests have no role in rural livelihoods
options.B: Forests support livelihoods through NTFPs, fuelwood and fodder where legally permitted, grazing arrangements, ecotourism, employment in conservation and watershed services, while access is governed by applicable forest and rights laws
options.C: Forests only provide timber for export
options.D: Forests are only used for recreational purposes

questions.explanation: Forests support livelihoods through NTFPs, fuelwood and fodder where legally permitted, grazing arrangements, ecotourism, employment in conservation and watershed services, while access is governed by applicable forest and rights laws.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which forest-based products are important in Karnataka?

options.A: Only timber
options.B: Bamboo, cane, honey, medicinal plants, tamarind, amla, soapnut, gums, resins, leaves and other locally collected NTFPs, subject to sustainable collection and applicable rights

questions.explanation: Examples of important forest-based products in Karnataka include bamboo, cane, honey, medicinal plants, tamarind, amla, soapnut, gums, resins, leaves and other locally collected NTFPs, subject to sustainable collection and applicable rights.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which mountain range is the most important forest-rich region of Karnataka?

options.A: The Eastern Ghats
options.B: The Western Ghats, which run along the State's western side and form part of a globally significant biodiversity hotspot

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats, which run along the State's western side, are Karnataka's most important forest-rich mountain region and form part of a globally significant biodiversity hotspot.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which UNESCO World Heritage property includes parts of Karnataka's Western Ghats?

options.A: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
options.B: The UNESCO World Heritage property known as the Western Ghats, which includes several component areas in Karnataka and extends across multiple States

questions.explanation: The UNESCO World Heritage property known as the Western Ghats includes several component areas in Karnataka; the property is serial and extends across multiple States.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which national parks are located in Karnataka?

options.A: Only Bandipur and Nagarahole
options.B: Major national parks include Bandipur, Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi), Bannerghatta, Kudremukh, Anshi (now within Kali Tiger Reserve landscape) and other notified park areas

questions.explanation: Major national parks in Karnataka include Bandipur, Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi), Bannerghatta, Kudremukh, Anshi (now within Kali Tiger Reserve landscape) and other notified park areas; check current official notifications for any administrative changes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which tiger reserves are located in Karnataka?

options.A: Only Bandipur and Bhadra
options.B: Karnataka's major tiger reserves include Bandipur, Bhadra, Kali, Nagarahole, Bilgiri Ranganatha Temple (BRT) and, following notification, other reserves such as Male Mahadeshwara Hills

questions.explanation: Karnataka's major tiger reserves include Bandipur, Bhadra, Kali, Nagarahole, Bilgiri Ranganatha Temple (BRT) and, following notification, other reserves such as Male Mahadeshwara Hills; use the latest National Tiger Conservation Authority list for current count and status.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which biosphere reserve includes parts of Karnataka?

options.A: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, which includes parts of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu and encompasses important forest landscapes including the Bandipur-Nagarahole region
options.C: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve

questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve includes parts of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu; it encompasses important forest landscapes including the Bandipur-Nagarahole region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which Karnataka forest landscape is associated with the Kudremukh National Park?

options.A: Kudremukh National Park lies in the Western Ghats, mainly in Chikkamagaluru district, with parts of the landscape adjoining Udupi and Dakshina Kannada regions
options.B: Kudremukh National Park lies in the Eastern Ghats
options.C: Kudremukh National Park lies in the Deccan plateau
options.D: Kudremukh National Park lies in the coastal plains

questions.explanation: Kudremukh National Park lies in the Western Ghats, mainly in Chikkamagaluru district, with parts of the landscape adjoining Udupi and Dakshina Kannada regions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why is the Kali Tiger Reserve important?

options.A: It protects Western Ghats forests and habitats associated with species such as tiger, leopard, elephant, gaur and several endemic plants and animals in Uttara Kannada district
options.B: It is located in the Eastern Ghats
options.C: It is the largest national park in India
options.D: It is a biosphere reserve only

questions.explanation: Kali Tiger Reserve in Uttara Kannada district protects Western Ghats forests and habitats associated with species such as tiger, leopard, elephant, gaur and several endemic plants and animals.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why are Bandipur and Nagarahole important?

options.A: They form part of the Nilgiri landscape, support important tiger and elephant populations and are connected to wider forest habitats across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala
options.B: They are located in the Eastern Ghats only
options.C: They are the only national parks in Karnataka

questions.explanation: Bandipur and Nagarahole form part of the Nilgiri landscape, support important tiger and elephant populations and are connected to wider forest habitats across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the significance of the Bilgiri Ranganatha Temple (BRT) Tiger Reserve?

options.A: BRT in Chamarajanagar district links the Eastern and Western Ghats landscapes and is important for biodiversity, tiger conservation and ecological connectivity
options.B: BRT is located in the Western Ghats only
options.C: BRT is the largest tiger reserve in India
options.D: BRT is a biosphere reserve only

questions.explanation: BRT in Chamarajanagar district links the Eastern and Western Ghats landscapes and is important for biodiversity, tiger conservation and ecological connectivity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the significance of the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary?

options.A: It protects riverine and dry-deciduous forest habitats along the Cauvery landscape in southern Karnataka and supports wildlife including elephants, leopards and river-associated species
options.B: It is located in the Western Ghats only
options.C: It is the largest national park in Karnataka
options.D: It is a biosphere reserve only

questions.explanation: The Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary protects riverine and dry-deciduous forest habitats along the Cauvery landscape in southern Karnataka and supports wildlife including elephants, leopards and river-associated species.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is deforestation?

options.A: A decline in forest quality without converting it to non-forest land use
options.B: The permanent or long-term conversion of forest land to non-forest land uses, such as agriculture, settlements, infrastructure, mining or industrial development
options.C: The planting of trees on non-forest land

questions.explanation: Deforestation is the permanent or long-term conversion of forest land to non-forest land uses, such as agriculture, settlements, infrastructure, mining or industrial development.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is forest degradation?

options.A: The complete conversion of forest land to non-forest use
options.B: A decline in the condition, structure, productivity or ecological functions of a forest without necessarily converting it completely to a non-forest land use
options.C: The planting of trees on non-forest land

questions.explanation: Forest degradation is a decline in the condition, structure, productivity or ecological functions of a forest without necessarily converting it completely to a non-forest land use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How is deforestation different from forest degradation?

options.A: Deforestation involves conversion or loss of forest land as forest, whereas degradation means the forest remains but its quality, biomass, biodiversity or ecological functioning declines
options.B: Deforestation and degradation are the same thing
options.C: Deforestation means decline in quality, degradation means complete conversion

questions.explanation: Deforestation involves conversion or loss of forest land as forest, whereas degradation means the forest remains but its quality, biomass, biodiversity or ecological functioning declines.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the major direct causes of deforestation?

options.A: Only natural disasters
options.B: Major direct causes include agricultural expansion, shifting cultivation where unsustainable, mining, dams, roads, urbanisation, industrial projects, logging, encroachment and conversion to plantations or other land uses

questions.explanation: Major direct causes include agricultural expansion, shifting cultivation where unsustainable, mining, dams, roads, urbanisation, industrial projects, logging, encroachment and conversion to plantations or other land uses.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can infrastructure projects cause deforestation?

options.A: Roads, railways, power lines, dams and other projects may require tree felling and land diversion and can fragment habitats, increase access and encourage further encroachment
options.B: Infrastructure projects have no impact on forests
options.D: Infrastructure projects always improve forest cover

questions.explanation: Roads, railways, power lines, dams and other projects may require tree felling and land diversion and can fragment habitats, increase access and encourage further encroachment.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can mining cause deforestation?

options.A: Mining can clear vegetation, remove topsoil, fragment habitats, create waste dumps and roads, and generate dust and polluted runoff that affect surrounding forests
options.B: Mining has no impact on forests

questions.explanation: Mining can clear vegetation, remove topsoil, fragment habitats, create waste dumps and roads, and generate dust and polluted runoff that affect surrounding forests.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can agriculture cause deforestation?

options.A: Agriculture has no impact on forests
options.B: Expansion of cropland, plantations and grazing land can replace natural forests and reduce habitat connectivity when not planned sustainably

questions.explanation: Expansion of cropland, plantations and grazing land can replace natural forests and reduce habitat connectivity when not planned sustainably.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is forest fragmentation?

options.A: The breaking of a continuous forest into smaller, isolated patches, often by roads, farms, settlements, mines or other land uses
options.B: The natural growth of a continuous forest
options.C: The planting of trees in a continuous block
options.D: The complete protection of a forest from human activity

questions.explanation: Forest fragmentation is the breaking of a continuous forest into smaller, isolated patches, often by roads, farms, settlements, mines or other land uses.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the edge effect in forests?

options.A: The change in environmental conditions and species composition near the boundary of a forest patch, often involving greater light, heat, wind and human disturbance
options.B: The growth of trees at the center of a forest
options.C: The complete protection of a forest boundary
options.D: The natural regeneration of forest edges

questions.explanation: The edge effect is the change in environmental conditions and species composition near the boundary of a forest patch, often involving greater light, heat, wind and human disturbance.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the environmental consequences of deforestation?

options.A: Only increased timber production

questions.question: What is afforestation?

options.A: Establishment of forest on land not recently under forest
options.B: Re-establishment of forest on previously forested land
options.C: Permanent conversion of forest to non-forest land use

questions.explanation: Afforestation is the establishment of forest on land not recently under forest.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is reforestation?

options.A: Establishment of forest on land not recently under forest
options.B: Re-establishment of forest on previously forested land
options.C: Permanent conversion of forest to non-forest land use

questions.explanation: Reforestation is the re-establishment of forest on previously forested land.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is deforestation?

options.A: Establishment of forest on land not recently under forest
options.B: Re-establishment of forest on previously forested land
options.C: Permanent conversion of forest to non-forest land use

questions.explanation: Deforestation is the permanent conversion of forest to non-forest land use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which forest type is prominent in the high-rainfall Western Ghats of Karnataka?

options.A: Tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests

questions.explanation: Tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests are prominent in the high-rainfall Western Ghats, especially in parts of Uttara Kannada, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru and Kodagu districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: In which region of Karnataka are moist deciduous forests found?

options.A: In the Malnad and wetter forest belts of the State
options.C: In the rain-shadow areas of north Karnataka

questions.explanation: Moist deciduous forests occur in parts of the Western Ghats and adjoining regions, including areas of the Malnad and the wetter forest belts of the State.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which forest type is found around Bandipur and other eastern forest divisions of Karnataka?

options.A: Dry deciduous forests

questions.explanation: Dry deciduous forests occur in the drier interior and eastern parts of Karnataka, including portions of the Deccan plateau and the forest landscapes around Bandipur and other eastern forest divisions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Where are shola-grassland ecosystems found in Karnataka?

options.A: In high-elevation landscapes of the Western Ghats, including parts of Kudremukh and adjoining high ranges
options.C: In the rain-shadow areas of north Karnataka

questions.explanation: Shola-grassland ecosystems occur in high-elevation landscapes of the Western Ghats, including parts of Kudremukh and adjoining high ranges.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which estuarine systems in Karnataka support mangroves?

options.A: Kali, Sharavathi and Netravati estuarine systems

questions.explanation: Mangroves occur in estuaries and sheltered coastal stretches of Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts, including parts of the Kali, Sharavathi, Netravati and other estuarine systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is an important NTFP in Karnataka?

options.A: Bamboo, cane, honey, medicinal plants, tamarind, amla and soapnut

questions.explanation: Examples of important forest-based products in Karnataka include bamboo, cane, honey, medicinal plants, tamarind, amla, soapnut, gums, resins, leaves and other locally collected NTFPs, subject to sustainable collection and applicable rights.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: The Western Ghats form part of which globally significant biodiversity hotspot?

options.A: The Western Ghats-Sri Lanka biodiversity hotspot

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats form part of a globally significant biodiversity hotspot; the Western Ghats-Sri Lanka region is one of the recognised global hotspots.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which national park in Karnataka is now within the Kali Tiger Reserve landscape?

options.A: Anshi National Park

questions.explanation: Anshi National Park is now within the Kali Tiger Reserve landscape.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which tiger reserve in Karnataka links the Eastern and Western Ghats landscapes?

options.A: Bilgiri Ranganatha Temple (BRT) Tiger Reserve

questions.explanation: BRT in Chamarajanagar district links the Eastern and Western Ghats landscapes and is important for biodiversity, tiger conservation and ecological connectivity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which biosphere reserve encompasses the Bandipur-Nagarahole region?

options.A: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve

questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve includes parts of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu; it encompasses important forest landscapes including the Bandipur-Nagarahole region.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Kudremukh National Park is mainly located in which district of Karnataka?

options.A: Chikkamagaluru district

questions.explanation: Kudremukh National Park lies in the Western Ghats, mainly in Chikkamagaluru district, with parts of the landscape adjoining Udupi and Dakshina Kannada regions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Kali Tiger Reserve is located in which district of Karnataka?

options.A: Uttara Kannada district

questions.explanation: Kali Tiger Reserve in Uttara Kannada district protects Western Ghats forests and habitats associated with species such as tiger, leopard, elephant, gaur and several endemic plants and animals.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: BRT Tiger Reserve is located in which district of Karnataka?

options.A: Chamarajanagar district

questions.explanation: BRT in Chamarajanagar district links the Eastern and Western Ghats landscapes and is important for biodiversity, tiger conservation and ecological connectivity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: The Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary protects which types of habitats?

options.A: Riverine and dry-deciduous forest habitats along the Cauvery landscape

questions.explanation: The Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary protects riverine and dry-deciduous forest habitats along the Cauvery landscape in southern Karnataka and supports wildlife including elephants, leopards and river-associated species.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is a direct cause of deforestation?

options.A: Agricultural expansion

questions.explanation: Major direct causes of deforestation include agricultural expansion, shifting cultivation where unsustainable, mining, dams, roads, urbanisation, industrial projects, logging, encroachment and conversion to plantations or other land uses.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental consequence of deforestation?

options.A: Biodiversity loss and habitat fragmentation

questions.explanation: Deforestation can cause biodiversity loss, habitat fragmentation, soil erosion, landslides, altered water flows, reduced carbon storage, local warming, increased human-wildlife conflict and loss of ecosystem services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why should afforestation use native species where ecologically appropriate?

options.A: Native species are generally better adapted to local ecological conditions and can support local biodiversity
options.B: Native species are always cheaper than exotic species
options.C: Native species grow faster than exotic species

questions.explanation: Native species are generally better adapted to local ecological conditions and can support local biodiversity; species selection must consider site conditions, water availability and restoration objectives.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why can monoculture plantations fail to replace natural forests?

options.A: Monocultures usually support fewer habitat types and species than diverse natural forests and may be more vulnerable to pests, disease, fire or climatic stress
options.B: Monocultures always support more biodiversity than natural forests
options.C: Monocultures are always more resilient than natural forests

questions.explanation: Monocultures usually support fewer habitat types and species than diverse natural forests and may be more vulnerable to pests, disease, fire or climatic stress; plantation area should not be treated as equivalent to natural-forest ecological quality.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Who developed the Miyawaki method?

options.A: Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki

questions.explanation: The Miyawaki method is a dense native-species planting approach developed by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, often used for small urban sites; its success depends on site suitability, species selection, soil preparation and long-term maintenance.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does CAMPA stand for?

options.A: Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority
options.B: Central Afforestation Management and Planning Agency
options.C: Conservation and Management of Protected Areas
options.D: Compensatory Afforestation Monitoring and Protection Authority

questions.explanation: CAMPA refers to the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority framework, which guides the management and use of funds collected for compensatory afforestation and related activities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 provides for the establishment of which funds?

options.A: National and State funds to manage money received for compensatory afforestation, additional compensatory afforestation, penal compensatory afforestation and related purposes

questions.explanation: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 provides for the establishment of national and State funds to manage money received for compensatory afforestation, additional compensatory afforestation, penal compensatory afforestation and related purposes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: The Green India Mission is one of India's missions under which framework?

options.A: The National Action Plan on Climate Change
options.B: The National Action Plan on Biodiversity
options.C: The National Action Plan on Desertification
options.D: The National Action Plan on Wildlife

questions.explanation: The National Mission for a Green India is one of India's missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change; it aims to protect, restore and enhance forest and tree cover and improve ecosystem services and livelihoods.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Joint Forest Management involves cooperation between which parties?

options.A: Forest departments and local communities
options.B: Only the central government and state governments
options.C: Only private companies and forest departments

questions.explanation: Joint Forest Management is an approach in which forest departments and local communities cooperate in protecting and managing forests, with benefit-sharing arrangements defined by State policies and local institutions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does forest conservation aim to maintain?

options.A: Biodiversity, ecological functions, natural resources and community livelihoods for present and future generations

questions.explanation: Forest conservation is the protection, sustainable management and restoration of forests to maintain biodiversity, ecological functions, natural resources and community livelihoods for present and future generations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the main difference between in-situ and ex-situ conservation?

options.A: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, while ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitats
options.B: In-situ and ex-situ conservation are the same
options.C: In-situ conservation protects species in zoos, while ex-situ conservation protects species in natural habitats
options.D: In-situ conservation only applies to plants

questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats through protected areas and other effective conservation measures. Ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitats, for example in botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks, zoos and tissue-culture facilities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act are national parks notified in India?

options.A: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972

questions.explanation: A national park is a legally notified protected area established to conserve wildlife and its habitat, with restrictions on activities as provided under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act are wildlife sanctuaries notified in India?

options.A: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972

questions.explanation: A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 to protect wildlife and habitat, with rights and permitted activities regulated under the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does a tiger reserve generally include?

options.A: Core or critical tiger habitat and a buffer area

questions.explanation: A tiger reserve is a landscape designated under the Wildlife (Protection) Act framework for tiger conservation, generally including core or critical tiger habitat and a buffer area.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the three zones commonly found in a biosphere reserve?

options.A: Core, buffer and transition zones

questions.explanation: A biosphere reserve is a large landscape designated to conserve biodiversity while promoting sustainable use and research; it commonly has core, buffer and transition zones.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the criteria for a biodiversity hotspot?

options.A: Exceptionally high plant endemism and severe habitat loss

questions.explanation: A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with exceptionally high plant endemism and severe habitat loss; the Western Ghats-Sri Lanka region is one of the recognised global hotspots.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What ecosystem services do the Western Ghats provide to Karnataka?

options.A: They regulate water flows into major river systems, store carbon and provide habitats and livelihoods

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats support high species richness and endemism, regulate water flows into major river systems, store carbon and provide habitats and livelihoods; they are also vulnerable to fragmentation, development pressure and climate risks.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 regulate?

options.A: The dereservation of forests and the use of forest land for non-forest purposes
options.D: The management of compensatory afforestation funds

questions.explanation: It regulates the dereservation of forests and the use of forest land for non-forest purposes, requiring prior Central Government approval for activities covered by the Act, subject to its scope and exemptions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which communities are eligible for rights under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?

options.A: Eligible forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 recognises and vests certain individual and community forest rights of eligible forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the three main objectives of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002?

options.A: Conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of benefits
options.C: Timber production, fuelwood collection and grazing

questions.explanation: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 provides for conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from biological resources and associated knowledge.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 regulate?

options.A: Protection of wild animals, birds and plants, establishment of protected areas, and hunting and wildlife trade

questions.explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 provides the legal framework for protection of wild animals, birds and plants and for establishing protected areas and regulating hunting and wildlife trade.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act framework does the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) function?

options.A: The Wildlife (Protection) Act

questions.explanation: NTCA is a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act framework that strengthens tiger conservation through standards, oversight, monitoring and support to tiger reserves.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Ministry does the Forest Survey of India function?

options.A: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.explanation: FSI, under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, assesses forest resources, publishes the biennial India State of Forest Report and provides forest-fire alerts and related information.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change oversee?

options.A: National environmental and forest policies, key forest and wildlife laws, national programmes and relevant institutions

questions.explanation: The Ministry formulates national environmental and forest policies, administers key forest and wildlife laws, coordinates national programmes and oversees relevant institutions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can local communities contribute to forest conservation?

options.A: Through participatory management, fire prevention, sustainable NTFP collection, biodiversity monitoring, restoration and reporting illegal activities
options.D: Local communities have no role in forest conservation

questions.explanation: Communities can help protect forests through participatory management, fire prevention, sustainable NTFP collection, biodiversity monitoring, restoration, reporting illegal activities and implementing recognised rights and responsibilities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why are sacred groves important for forest conservation?

options.A: They can conserve native species, genetic resources, water sources and small habitat refuges
options.C: They are areas where all trees are cut

questions.explanation: Sacred groves are community-protected forest patches preserved for cultural or religious reasons; they can conserve native species, genetic resources, water sources and small habitat refuges.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act framework are Biodiversity Management Committees constituted?

options.A: The Biological Diversity Act

questions.explanation: A Biodiversity Management Committee is a local-level body constituted under the Biological Diversity Act framework to promote conservation, sustainable use and documentation of local biological resources and associated knowledge.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does a People's Biodiversity Register record?

options.A: Biological resources and associated traditional knowledge prepared through participatory processes

questions.explanation: A People's Biodiversity Register is a local record of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge prepared through participatory processes under the biodiversity governance framework.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Is an eco-sensitive zone automatically a complete no-development zone?

options.A: No, it is not automatically a complete no-development zone; activities are regulated according to the applicable notification
options.C: Yes, all human activity is prohibited
options.D: Eco-sensitive zones do not regulate any activities

questions.explanation: An eco-sensitive zone is an area around or near a protected area notified under environmental law to regulate specified activities and reduce adverse pressures on the protected ecosystem; it is not automatically a complete no-development zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the purpose of an elephant corridor?

options.A: To enable elephants to move between habitat areas and reduce fragmentation

questions.explanation: An elephant corridor is a landscape link that enables elephants to move between habitat areas; protecting corridors reduces fragmentation and can help lower conflict when combined with land-use and community measures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is a major threat to forests in Karnataka?

options.A: Habitat fragmentation

questions.explanation: Major threats include habitat fragmentation, encroachment, mining and quarrying, linear infrastructure, invasive alien species, forest fires, unsustainable extraction, grazing pressure in some areas, human-wildlife conflict and climate change.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What makes the Western Ghats region of Karnataka ecologically sensitive?

options.A: High biodiversity and endemism, steep slopes, headwaters and important evergreen and semi-evergreen forests

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats region contains high biodiversity and endemism, steep slopes, headwaters and important evergreen and semi-evergreen forests; poorly planned land-use change can cause erosion, landslides, fragmentation and loss of ecosystem services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which states share the Nilgiri landscape that is important for Karnataka forest conservation?

options.A: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala

questions.explanation: The Nilgiri landscape connects forest habitats across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala and supports large mammals, including tigers and elephants, making landscape-scale coordination important.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which large mammals are supported by the Bandipur-Nagarahole landscape?

options.A: Tiger and elephant populations

questions.explanation: The Bandipur-Nagarahole landscape is part of a larger connected forest landscape that supports tiger and elephant populations and requires habitat connectivity, fire management and measures to reduce human-wildlife conflict.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Kali landscape protect in Karnataka?

options.A: Important Western Ghats forest ecosystems in Uttara Kannada, biodiversity, river catchments and wildlife connectivity

questions.explanation: The Kali landscape protects important Western Ghats forest ecosystems in Uttara Kannada and supports biodiversity, river catchments and wildlife connectivity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: The BRT landscape is an important ecological link between which two regions?

options.A: The Eastern and Western Ghats
options.B: The coastal plains and the Deccan plateau
options.C: The Malnad and the coastal plains

questions.explanation: The Bilgiri Ranganatha Temple landscape is an important ecological link between the Eastern and Western Ghats and supports forest-dependent communities and wildlife.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can projects minimise adverse impacts on forests in Karnataka?

options.A: By avoiding ecologically sensitive areas where feasible, assessing cumulative impacts, minimising fragmentation, maintaining wildlife corridors, complying with forest and wildlife laws, consulting affected communities and ensuring credible restoration and monitoring
options.C: By converting all forests to agriculture
options.D: By removing all forest protection laws

questions.explanation: Projects should avoid ecologically sensitive areas where feasible, assess cumulative impacts, minimise fragmentation, maintain wildlife corridors, comply with forest and wildlife laws, consult affected communities and ensure credible restoration and monitoring.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the three types of forest fires mentioned in the study material?

options.A: Surface, ground and crown fires

questions.explanation: A forest fire is an uncontrolled or unwanted fire that burns vegetation in a forest or other natural landscape; it may be surface, ground or crown fire.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which type of forest fire burns organic matter below the surface, such as peat, humus or partially decomposed material?

options.A: Ground fire

questions.explanation: A ground fire burns organic matter below the surface, such as peat, humus or partially decomposed material, and may smoulder for long periods.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which type of forest fire spreads through the upper canopy of trees and can move rapidly?

options.A: Crown fire

questions.explanation: A crown fire spreads through the upper canopy of trees and can move rapidly, especially under dry, windy conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is an important natural ignition source for forest fires?

options.A: Lightning

questions.explanation: Lightning is an important natural ignition source; under suitable conditions, prolonged drought, heat and dry vegetation allow fires to spread.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is a human cause of forest fires in India?

options.A: Discarded smoking materials

questions.explanation: Human causes include deliberate burning, escaped agricultural or pasture fires, discarded smoking materials, unattended campfires, burning for collection or access, and sparks from machinery or infrastructure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why does dry season increase forest fire risk?

options.A: Dry leaves, grasses and branches accumulate and lose moisture, making vegetation easier to ignite and allowing fires to spread

questions.explanation: Dry leaves, grasses and branches accumulate and lose moisture during the dry season, making vegetation easier to ignite and allowing fires to spread.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What materials contribute to fuel load in a forest?

options.A: Dry grass, leaves, twigs and dead wood

questions.explanation: Fuel load is the amount of combustible material, such as dry grass, leaves, twigs and dead wood, available to burn in a given area.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which weather factors influence ignition and fire spread?

options.A: Temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and rainfall or drought conditions

questions.explanation: Fire weather refers to weather conditions that influence ignition and fire spread, especially temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and rainfall or drought conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How does wind accelerate forest fires?

options.A: Wind supplies oxygen, bends flames toward unburned vegetation, carries embers and can accelerate the spread and intensity of fires
options.D: Wind has no effect on fires

questions.explanation: Wind supplies oxygen, bends flames toward unburned vegetation, carries embers and can accelerate the spread and intensity of fires.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can forest fires affect biodiversity?

options.A: Fires can kill plants and animals, destroy nests and habitat, alter species composition, damage soil organisms and threaten rare or fire-sensitive species
options.D: Fires have no effect on biodiversity

questions.explanation: Fires can kill plants and animals, destroy nests and habitat, alter species composition, damage soil organisms and threaten rare or fire-sensitive species; some ecosystems are adapted to periodic low-intensity fire, so impacts depend on fire regime.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can severe fires affect soil?

options.A: They can remove protective vegetation and litter, alter soil structure, reduce infiltration, increase erosion and cause nutrient loss
options.D: They have no effect on soil

questions.explanation: Severe fires can remove protective vegetation and litter, alter soil structure, reduce infiltration, increase erosion and cause nutrient loss; intense heat can also create water-repellent soil layers in some conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can forest fires affect water resources?

options.A: Burned catchments may experience greater runoff, sediment movement and ash transport into streams and reservoirs, reducing water quality and increasing siltation
options.D: Fires have no effect on water resources

questions.explanation: Burned catchments may experience greater runoff, sediment movement and ash transport into streams and reservoirs, reducing water quality and increasing siltation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which pollutants are released by forest fires?

options.A: Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, methane, particulate matter and other pollutants

questions.explanation: Fires release carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, methane, particulate matter and other pollutants; smoke can cause respiratory and cardiovascular harm and contribute to short-term climate forcing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under what conditions is a prescribed burn applied?

options.A: Under specified weather, fuel and safety conditions to achieve defined management objectives, where legally authorised and ecologically appropriate
options.B: Under any weather conditions without planning

questions.explanation: A prescribed burn is a planned fire applied under specified weather, fuel and safety conditions to achieve defined management objectives, where legally authorised and ecologically appropriate.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the purpose of a fire line?

options.A: To slow or stop the spread of a fire by removing or reducing combustible vegetation or material
options.B: To plant trees after a fire
options.D: To serve as a road for fire engines

questions.explanation: A fire line is a strip in which combustible vegetation or material is removed or reduced to slow or stop the spread of a fire.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the purpose of a firebreak?

options.A: To interrupt fuel continuity and help contain a fire
options.B: To plant trees after a fire
options.D: To serve as a road for fire engines

questions.explanation: A firebreak is a barrier or cleared strip designed to interrupt fuel continuity and help contain a fire.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which methods are used for early detection of forest fires?

options.A: Watchtowers, patrols, community reporting, cameras, satellites and alert systems

questions.explanation: Early detection is the identification of a fire soon after ignition using watchtowers, patrols, community reporting, cameras, satellites and alert systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How does the Forest Survey of India provide forest-fire alerts?

options.A: Using satellite-based monitoring and related systems

questions.explanation: The Forest Survey of India provides forest-fire alerts using satellite-based monitoring and related systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can local communities help prevent forest fires?

options.A: By reporting smoke and ignition quickly, avoiding unsafe burning, helping maintain fire lines, participating in awareness programmes and coordinating with forest staff

questions.explanation: Local communities can report smoke and ignition quickly, avoid unsafe burning, help maintain fire lines where appropriate, participate in awareness programmes and coordinate with forest staff during authorised response operations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is a method of forest-fire prevention?

options.A: Reducing hazardous fuel accumulation where ecologically suitable

questions.explanation: Methods include reducing hazardous fuel accumulation where ecologically suitable, maintaining fire lines, regulating human activities during high-risk periods, public awareness, early-warning systems, patrols and community participation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What should people avoid doing when they see a forest fire?

options.A: Attempting to fight a large or fast-moving fire
options.B: Moving away from the fire and smoke
options.D: Informing the Forest Department or emergency services

questions.explanation: They should move away from the fire and smoke, avoid attempting to fight a large or fast-moving fire, warn others if safe, and immediately inform the Forest Department or emergency services with the location and direction of spread.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why is it dangerous to enter a forest during a fire?

options.A: Fire fronts and smoke can change direction rapidly, and falling trees, embers, poor visibility and toxic smoke can cause serious injury or death
options.C: Cameras do not work during fires
options.D: There is no danger in entering a forest during a fire

questions.explanation: Fire fronts and smoke can change direction rapidly, and falling trees, embers, poor visibility and toxic smoke can cause serious injury or death.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which forest types in Karnataka are vulnerable to seasonal fires?

options.A: Dry deciduous and scrub forests, as well as grassland and forest mosaics in the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Dry deciduous and scrub forests in parts of southern and eastern Karnataka, as well as grassland and forest mosaics in the Western Ghats, can face seasonal fire risk; risk varies with rainfall, fuel and local conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What factors create fire risk in the Bandipur landscape during dry years?

options.A: Dry-season vegetation, accumulated grass and leaf litter, high temperatures, wind and human ignition sources

questions.explanation: Dry-season vegetation, accumulated grass and leaf litter, high temperatures, wind and human ignition sources can combine to create conditions for rapid fire spread in the Bandipur landscape.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why must fire management in the Western Ghats consider different habitats?

options.A: Fire ecology differs among habitats; repeated fires can alter shola-grassland mosaics, favour invasive species and damage fire-sensitive evergreen forests
options.B: All Western Ghats habitats are adapted to frequent fires
options.C: Fires always improve Western Ghats forests
options.D: Fire management is not important in the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Fire management must prevent damaging human-caused fires while recognising that fire ecology differs among habitats; repeated fires can alter shola-grassland mosaics, favour invasive species and damage fire-sensitive evergreen forests.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is a forest fire control measure in Karnataka?

options.A: Seasonal fire preparedness and satellite alerts

questions.explanation: Control measures include seasonal fire preparedness, satellite alerts, local patrols, maintained fire lines, trained response teams, community reporting, access to water and equipment, and post-fire ecological assessment.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the frequency of the India State of Forest Report?

options.A: Biennial (every two years)

questions.question: Where are shola-grassland ecosystems found in Karnataka?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is a direct cause of deforestation?

options.A: Agricultural expansion

questions.explanation: Major direct causes of deforestation include agricultural expansion, shifting cultivation where unsustainable, mining, dams, roads, urbanisation, industrial projects, logging, encroachment and conversion to plantations or other land uses.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental consequence of deforestation?

options.A: Biodiversity loss and habitat fragmentation

questions.explanation: Deforestation can cause biodiversity loss, habitat fragmentation, soil erosion, landslides, altered water flows, reduced carbon storage, local warming, increased human-wildlife conflict and loss of ecosystem services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why should afforestation use native species where ecologically appropriate?

options.A: Native species are generally better adapted to local ecological conditions and can support local biodiversity
options.B: Native species are always cheaper than exotic species
options.C: Native species grow faster than exotic species

questions.explanation: Native species are generally better adapted to local ecological conditions and can support local biodiversity; species selection must consider site conditions, water availability and restoration objectives.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why can monoculture plantations fail to replace natural forests?

options.A: Monocultures usually support fewer habitat types and species than diverse natural forests and may be more vulnerable to pests, disease, fire or climatic stress
options.B: Monocultures always support more biodiversity than natural forests
options.C: Monocultures are always more resilient than natural forests

questions.explanation: Monocultures usually support fewer habitat types and species than diverse natural forests and may be more vulnerable to pests, disease, fire or climatic stress; plantation area should not be treated as equivalent to natural-forest ecological quality.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Who developed the Miyawaki method?

options.A: Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki

questions.explanation: The Miyawaki method is a dense native-species planting approach developed by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, often used for small urban sites; its success depends on site suitability, species selection, soil preparation and long-term maintenance.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does CAMPA stand for?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does forest conservation aim to maintain?

options.A: Biodiversity, ecological functions, natural resources and community livelihoods for present and future generations

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What is the main difference between in-situ and ex-situ conservation?

options.A: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, while ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitats
options.B: In-situ and ex-situ conservation are the same
options.C: In-situ conservation protects species in zoos, while ex-situ conservation protects species in natural habitats
options.D: In-situ conservation only applies to plants

questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats through protected areas and other effective conservation measures. Ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitats, for example in botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks, zoos and tissue-culture facilities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act are national parks notified in India?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act are wildlife sanctuaries notified in India?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does a tiger reserve generally include?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the three zones commonly found in a biosphere reserve?

options.A: Core, buffer and transition zones

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the criteria for a biodiversity hotspot?

options.A: Exceptionally high plant endemism and severe habitat loss

questions.explanation: A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with exceptionally high plant endemism and severe habitat loss; the Western Ghats-Sri Lanka region is one of the recognised global hotspots.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What ecosystem services do the Western Ghats provide to Karnataka?

options.A: They regulate water flows into major river systems, store carbon and provide habitats and livelihoods

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats support high species richness and endemism, regulate water flows into major river systems, store carbon and provide habitats and livelihoods; they are also vulnerable to fragmentation, development pressure and climate risks.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 regulate?

questions.question: Which communities are eligible for rights under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What are the three main objectives of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002?

options.A: Conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of benefits

questions.explanation: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 provides for conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from biological resources and associated knowledge.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 regulate?

options.A: Protection of wild animals, birds and plants, establishment of protected areas, and hunting and wildlife trade

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act framework does the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) function?

questions.question: Under which Ministry does the Forest Survey of India function?

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: What does the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change oversee?

options.A: National environmental and forest policies, key forest and wildlife laws, national programmes and relevant institutions

questions.explanation: The Ministry formulates national environmental and forest policies, administers key forest and wildlife laws, coordinates national programmes and oversees relevant institutions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: How can local communities contribute to forest conservation?

options.A: Through participatory management, fire prevention, sustainable NTFP collection, biodiversity monitoring, restoration and reporting illegal activities

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Why are sacred groves important for forest conservation?

options.A: They can conserve native species, genetic resources, water sources and small habitat refuges

questions.explanation: Sacred groves are community-protected forest patches preserved for cultural or religious reasons; they can conserve native species, genetic resources, water sources and small habitat refuges.

questions.subject: Karnataka Forests
questions.question: Under which Act framework are Biodiversity Management Committees constituted?
